insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has generated 8,699 cryptographically verified purchase receipts — deterministic proof of transaction, not inferred intent. At a time when the ad industry pays $5+ CPM to guess who might buy, these signals confirm who already did.

insights.topic: Weekly GMV run rate doubling in six days
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV window went from $53K on April 1 to $101,734 on April 7 — a near-doubling in six days, now confirmed above the $100K weekly threshold after two failed attempts. The trailing two weeks account for 36% of all-time GMV, meaning recent throughput is structurally outpacing cumulative history.

A single 4-hour cycle on April 6 added $55,679 in GMV at an implied $1,031 per receipt — and the elevated average ticket held in subsequent cycles, with retail/department stores now averaging $172/receipt across 398 receipts in the 14-day window. This is a category-level structural shift in the receipt mix, not a one-cycle spike.

insights.topic: Velocity regime change: growth now compounding
insights.insight: Token velocity crossed above 1.0x for the first time on April 2 after 15+ consecutive cycles below threshold, and has held above 1.0x with acceleration also above 1.0x for three consecutive cycles. The network is growing faster than its trailing baseline, and that growth rate is itself expanding.

The April 6 heartbeat recorded 22 new CBSAs entering the signal window in a single cycle — the highest single-heartbeat count observed — with explicit non-metro coverage across WA, OK, IA, WI, MO, KS, HI, and 13 others. For brands targeting rural and secondary-market consumers, this is a verified purchase signal set that probabilistic platforms structurally underserve.

insights.topic: Category signal mix: grocery volume, retail value
insights.insight: In the trailing 14 days, grocery leads in receipt count (498 receipts) but retail/department stores leads in GMV weight ($68,401 vs. $34,482) at roughly double the per-receipt average. Brands in high-ticket categories are seeing disproportionate signal density relative to transaction volume.
